summary: F1–F4 are fixed. The rollout scripts now check against SOURCE_SHA, production.json bootstraps at 0.1.68, gcp discovery is limited to the west stack, and the temp tests run the real scripts. One new P1 remains: a PR that edits only Pulumi.prod.yaml always fails promote.yml validation. The coverage gate also still fails on promoteRelease.mjs:97.

findings.body: promote.yml runs on pull requests that touch `infra/control-plane/Pulumi.prod.yaml`, even when `releases/production.json` is unchanged. In that case the base and head production.json hold the same version. This step still sets `deploy=true` and passes the base file as `previous`, so `validatePromotion` returns `0.1.68 must be newer than production 0.1.68`. The `Find the staging release` step also looks up a halo-staging release for the current production version, which may not exist (0.1.68 does not). As a result, every ordinary prod infrastructure change, such as a new secret ID or domain setting, fails this check, and the Pulumi preview is skipped. Decide `deploy` and the version comparison by whether production.json changed between BASE_SHA and HEAD, for example with `git diff --quiet "$BASE_SHA" HEAD -- releases/production.json`. When it is unchanged, check only that Pulumi.prod.yaml still pins the current version, and still run the preview.

testRequests.target: releases/promoteRelease.mjs:97: a `run` subprocess exits non-zero, for example the gh stub fails `pr create` or `git push` is rejected. Assert exit status 1 and the message `<command> exited with status N`.
testRequests.rationale: This line is the only changed executable line still uncovered, so the coverage gate fails. The failure path also matters, because it leaves the user on the promote branch.
